messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed in the entire observable universe is the exoplanet **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × the radius of Jupiter** (about 18,000 km). This makes it the biggest planet we’ve been able to measure so far. (There are a few other very large candidates, but HD 100546 b is the most massive that has been confirmed.)

But the largest known exoplanet is HD 100546 b. Alternatively, the largest known exoplanet is HD 100546 b. But the question might be answered with "Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system."
